### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **48** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/test-typecheck-debt.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 216b18a6ccb47dc23d3fe9f6a8575daf54f25dd5`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/test-typecheck-debt.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 49 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 216b18a6ccb47dc23d3fe9f6a8575daf54f25dd5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ea9ffdd4d06e6542fef79a4b6fb7861636b40735` — the merge of head `00c88e7ef8ddfbbdf7d27473501b2fd69ad1e408` into base `216b18a6ccb47dc23d3fe9f6a8575daf54f25dd5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ea9ffdd4d06e6542fef79a4b6fb7861636b40735 && git checkout ea9ffdd4d06e6542fef79a4b6fb7861636b40735
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 216b18a6ccb47dc23d3fe9f6a8575daf54f25dd5 00c88e7ef8ddfbbdf7d27473501b2fd69ad1e408 && git checkout -B drift-repro 216b18a6ccb47dc23d3fe9f6a8575daf54f25dd5 && git merge --no-ff 00c88e7ef8ddfbbdf7d27473501b2fd69ad1e408

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 216b18a6ccb47dc23d3fe9f6a8575daf54f25dd5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 216b18a6ccb47dc23d3fe9f6a8575daf54f25dd5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `00c88e7ef8ddfbbdf7d27473501b2fd69ad1e408`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-lockout-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-sign-in-lockout.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts, the four plugin-auth test files, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/auth/signInRefusalMessages.ts, the 11 locale packs, .changeset/28381-lockout-uniform-answer-reset-clears.md + packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts (`update` returns a row count for `multi`, read), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts (`failed_login_count` default 0, read)

Tier note: the face is a declared widening (`AuthManagerOptions.lockoutRefusal`), so its tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The maintainer's standing order of 2026-11-04 pauses that tier for this project, so this record is served at `TIER_DEFAULT` and says so; it is the deviation, not a claim of the higher tier.

### ① Derived judgments

- Uniform refusal: the gate only records a verdict in a better-auth request-state slot; the password verifier handed to better-auth runs the real verification in full and then answers "no match" while the verdict is `locked`. So a locked account is refused by the endpoint's own wrong-password path (same status, body, one derivation), not by a mirror of it. Other endpoints that call `verify` see no verdict (the slot is set only by the `/sign-in/email` gate, per request), so their behaviour is unchanged.
- Atomic counting: each attempt reserves `failed_login_count` +1 by compare-and-set (`where: { id, failed_login_count: expected }`, `multi: true`; the engine contract returns a row count) and stamps `locked_until` in the same write at the threshold. Concurrency is pinned (30 parallel wrong passwords: exactly the threshold reach the check). Lost rounds re-read; after 32 lost rounds it fails closed (`locked`).
- NULL counter (seat review item): a NULL or absent counter matches the compare-and-set on the in-memory engine and on ObjectQL + SqlDriver (sqlite), tested with the column read back as NULL first; without that the account would read as locked forever.
- Reset clears: `onPasswordReset` clears counter and lock after the new password is written, on the emailed link and the phone code (tested); an incomplete reset clears nothing; the 2FA lock is untouched (admin Unlock still clears both).
- Settlement: success clears; a refusal after the credential passed (IP list, ban, unverified address) hands the reservation back; a locked refusal is neither counted twice nor cleared.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@object-ui/i18n`, `@object-ui/app-shell` under the repo's `fixed` changeset group: accepted. `packages/spec` untouched, `Metadata-protocol: none`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Widening: one new optional constructor key, `lockoutRefusal: 'uniform' | 'explicit'`, default `'uniform'`. The default changes the wire answer for a locked account from `403 ACCOUNT_LOCKED` to `401 INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD`; that is the card's security ask (it removes an account-existence oracle). Callers that keyed on `ACCOUNT_LOCKED`: the console copy is updated in all 11 locales; cloud already rewrites the answer on both planes (cloud#3422) and drops its rewrite after a pin round (follow-up owed, carrier cloud).
- Outside the endpoint pipeline (no request state) the gate still refuses with `403 ACCOUNT_LOCKED` and logs a degradation; better-auth opens a request state for the router and every `auth.api` call, so HTTP callers always get the uniform answer. Accepted as stated in the body.
- Residual, not a regression: an unknown address does no counter write while an existing one does one compare-and-set write; the old after-hook also wrote for existing accounts only. The scrypt cost, which dominates, is equal and pinned.
- Generated/ratchet files outside the package (census page + counts twin, engine-double ledger, test-typecheck debt down 16) are each written by their own tool. PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write). Not governed (`check-governed-merges`, 1305 lines).

### ④ Design judgment

- The design is the smallest one that makes the refusal identical by construction rather than by imitation, and it keeps the vendor's check order untouched. Acceptance items 1–4 of the card hold at this head; the reverse run (sources restored to `eff90af6`) turns the endpoint pins red.
- Out of scope, noted for the seat: `INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD` is not in the ADR-0112 error-code ledger; registering it would let the no-request-state fallback answer uniformly too. cloud follow-up: drop cloud#3422's rewrite after a pin round carrying this change.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-jhyfw5`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QUs3BvRcDHXqRU4TSVE4u6`

**VERDICT: PASS**
